articles.title: Sign in and check your laboratory
articles.summary: Sign in with your personal account and check your active laboratory and role before starting work.
articles.quick: Sign in with your username, replace any temporary password with a 12-character personal password, and check the top bar to confirm your laboratory and role.
before: Get your username and temporary password from your Laboratory Manager or administrator.
Check which laboratory name you are assigned to before entering any sample data.

steps.action: Open the sign-in screen, enter your Username or ID and password, and click Secure Sign In.
steps.expected: If you are using a temporary password, the Security Update Required dialog opens right away.

steps.action: Set a personal password of at least 12 characters, sign in again, and check your laboratory name and role in the top bar.
steps.expected: Your Dashboard opens with the side menu matching your assigned role.

steps.action: If your laboratory uses shared bench computers with PIN confirmation, open My Profile and set your personal 4 to 6 digit PIN.
steps.expected: Your personal PIN is saved and ready when you record results on a shared bench computer.

fields: Laboratory name
Active laboratory shown in the top bar
Confirm it matches your physical lab before entering samples or results.
Role & Scope
Your assigned role such as Laboratory Technician or Sample Reception Officer
Controls which menu items and approval buttons are available to you.
My Profile
Personal account settings page in the side menu
Use this page to change your password, language, or shared-bench PIN.
articles.example: Sign in as technician Amina on Demo Soil Lab, set a 12-character password, check "Demo Soil Lab" and "Laboratory Technician" in the top bar, and save a 4-digit PIN in My Profile.
articles.success: You are signed in under your own name with the right laboratory and role active.
articles.nextActor: Sample Reception Officer, Laboratory Technician, Quality & Audit Officer, or Laboratory Manager

problems.symptom: Your account signs in, but the wrong laboratory name appears in the top bar.
problems.why: Your account is assigned to a different facility or your role assignment has not been updated yet.
problems.action: Stop before entering any data and ask your Laboratory Manager to update your laboratory assignment in Laboratory Staff.

steps: Open the sign-in screen, enter your Username or ID and password, and click Secure Sign In. (Expected: If you are using a temporary password, the Security Update Required dialog opens right away.)

Set a personal password of at least 12 characters, sign in again, and check your laboratory name and role in the top bar. (Expected: Your Dashboard opens with the side menu matching your assigned role.)

If your laboratory uses shared bench computers with PIN confirmation, open My Profile and set your personal 4 to 6 digit PIN. (Expected: Your personal PIN is saved and ready when you record results on a shared bench computer.)
articles.caution: Never enter sample or bench results under a colleague's account or under the wrong laboratory name.

articles.title: Signing in and passwords
articles.summary: Sign in with a temporary password, set a 12-character personal password, handle paused sign-in attempts, and request an administrator password reset.
articles.quick: New passwords need at least 12 characters. On your first sign-in with a temporary password, the app asks you to set your own password. After several wrong attempts, your account is paused for a short time—wait and try again, or ask your lab admin to reset your password.
before: Have your assigned username and, for a new or reset account, the temporary password provided by your Laboratory Manager or administrator.
Prepare a personal password that is at least 12 characters long and different from your temporary or previous password.

sections.title: 1. First sign-in with a temporary password

steps.action: Open the sign-in screen, enter your Username or ID and your temporary password, and click Secure Sign In.
steps.expected: The Security Update Required dialog opens immediately and asks you to set a personal password before opening any lab screens.

steps.action: Enter your Current Temporary Password, type a New Private Password of at least 12 characters, confirm the new password, and click Update & Access System.
steps.expected: A Password Changed confirmation appears; click Log In Again and sign in with your new personal password.

sections.title: 2. Changing your password or recovering access

steps.action: To change your own password later, open My Profile, enter your current password and a new password of at least 12 characters, and click Save Changes.
steps.expected: Your password is updated and must be different from your previous password.

steps.action: If sign-in fails after several wrong attempts or you forget your password, wait a short time before trying again, or click Forgot password? and contact your Laboratory Manager. For manager or administrator access, contact your system administrator through your organization's usual support channel.
steps.expected: After a brief pause you can sign in again with the right password, or an administrator can issue a new temporary password from Laboratory Staff.

fields: New Private Password
Minimum 12 characters and different from your previous password
Required on first sign-in with a temporary password, after an admin reset, and when changing your password in My Profile.
Security Update Required
Password update dialog shown on first sign-in or after a reset
Keeps workspace access locked until you replace the temporary password and sign in again.
Reset Password
Administrator password reset in Laboratory Staff
Staff ask their Laboratory Manager for a reset; managers and administrators should contact their system administrator through their organization's usual support channel.
articles.example: Sign in with a temporary password, complete the Security Update Required dialog with a new 12-character password, click Log In Again, and sign in to your laboratory workspace.
articles.success: You can sign in with your personal 12-character password and know how to wait out a short sign-in pause or request an administrator reset.
articles.nextActor: Laboratory Staff User, Laboratory Manager, or System Administrator

problems.symptom: Sign-in keeps showing Invalid credentials. Please try again. after several wrong attempts.
problems.why: After several wrong attempts in a row, the account is paused for a short time to protect access, or the password typed does not match.
problems.action: Stop retrying right away, wait a short time, and try again carefully—or ask your Laboratory Manager to click Reset Password for your account in Laboratory Staff.

Enter your Current Temporary Password, type a New Private Password of at least 12 characters, confirm the new password, and click Update & Access System. (Expected: A Password Changed confirmation appears; click Log In Again and sign in with your new personal password.)

To change your own password later, open My Profile, enter your current password and a new password of at least 12 characters, and click Save Changes. (Expected: Your password is updated and must be different from your previous password.)

For manager or administrator access, contact your system administrator through your organization's usual support channel. articles.title: Your first shift as a technician
articles.summary: Follow your assigned samples from drying and preparation through bench testing and sending results for review.
articles.quick: Open My Work or Workbench, complete any open drying and preparation checks first, record your batch measurements and quality control samples, and send the finished work to your reviewer.
before: Check the top bar to confirm your laboratory name and Laboratory Technician role.
Have your bench worksheet, sample jars, and instrument calibration check ready.

steps.action: Open My Work or Workbench and check the tasks assigned to you for today.
steps.expected: You see which samples need Air Drying or Sample Preparation and which samples are ready for bench analysis.

steps.action: Finish any required drying and sieving checklists first and click Confirm Complete, then open your analysis worksheet or click New Analytical Run.
steps.expected: Confirmed preparation unlocks the test rows so you can type or paste sample results and quality control readings.

steps.action: Click Review Completion to record your checked results, then open Ready to Submit and click Submit.
steps.expected: Your recorded results move to Sent & Completed and appear in the reviewer's Manager Task List.

fields: My Work
Personal task list showing your assigned samples and runs
Start here each morning to see overdue, returned, or newly assigned work.
Checklist Verified
Green receipt badge shown after you click Confirm Complete on drying or preparation
Confirms that pre-analytical preparation is complete and bench tests can begin.
Ready to Submit
Handoff tab in Workbench for sending recorded results to a reviewer
Saving or recording a result keeps it on your bench until you submit it here.
articles.example: On Demo Soil Lab, confirm Air Drying and 2 mm Sample Preparation for five soil bags, enter their pH readings in Workbench, record the determinations, and submit them in Ready to Submit.
articles.success: Your preparation receipts and analytical results are recorded and visible in the reviewer queue.
articles.nextActor: Quality & Audit Officer or Laboratory Manager in Manager Task List

problems.symptom: You typed results into the worksheet, but your manager cannot see them in Manager Task List.
problems.why: The values were saved as a draft or recorded on the bench, but were not sent from Ready to Submit.
problems.action: Open Workbench, complete Review Completion if needed, then open Ready to Submit and click Submit.

steps: Open My Work or Workbench and check the tasks assigned to you for today. (Expected: You see which samples need Air Drying or Sample Preparation and which samples are ready for bench analysis.)

Finish any required drying and sieving checklists first and click Confirm Complete, then open your analysis worksheet or click New Analytical Run. (Expected: Confirmed preparation unlocks the test rows so you can type or paste sample results and quality control readings.)

Click Review Completion to record your checked results, then open Ready to Submit and click Submit. (Expected: Your recorded results move to Sent & Completed and appear in the reviewer's Manager Task List.)
articles.caution: Saving a draft worksheet does not send results to your manager. Always complete Review Completion and Ready to Submit at the end of a run.

articles.title: Your first shift at the intake desk
articles.summary: Follow the intake desk workflow: find expected samples, check bag condition and weight, assign analyses, print labels, and hand over to preparation.
articles.quick: Open Sample Reception, match the physical bag label to the project or consignment record, record weight and condition in 2. Condition, confirm requested tests in 3. Analyses, and complete intake in 4. Handover.
before: Confirm you are signed in as a Sample Reception Officer or Laboratory Manager.
Check that the bench scale is zeroed and the barcode label printer is loaded.

steps.action: Open Sample Reception, choose Project Sample, Walk-in / External, or Consignment Batch, and scan or type the bag ID in 1. ID & Field.
steps.expected: If the sample was pre-registered from a field survey, its status shows Expected and its field details load automatically.

steps.action: Weigh the soil bag and complete 2. Condition by checking Container Intact / Sealed and Sample Quantity Sufficient.
steps.expected: Any damaged bag or low sample weight is flagged so you can add a condition note, quarantine the bag, or reject it.

steps.action: Verify the requested test package in 3. Analyses, then open 4. Handover and click Complete Intake (or Accept & Print Label).
steps.expected: The sample status moves from Expected to Accepted, barcode labels print, and drying tasks open in Workbench.

fields: Expected
Status of a sample synced from a field form before the bag arrives
Never confirm intake until the physical soil bag is on your desk.
2. Condition
Reception compliance step for weight, seal, and moisture checks
Record actual weight in grams and select Pass or Fail for each check.
Complete Intake
Final confirmation button in 4. Handover
Assigns the official lab ID, records the reception timestamp, and opens preparation tasks.
articles.example: Scan bag FIELD-2026-001 in Sample Reception, record 620 g in intact condition, select the routine fertility package, and click Complete Intake (or Accept & Print Label).
articles.success: The sample is accepted with a printed barcode label and appears in the drying and preparation queue.
articles.nextActor: Laboratory Technician in drying and sample preparation

problems.symptom: A sample synced from a field survey does not appear in Received Today or on technician workbenches.
problems.why: Field sync only creates an Expected record; samples do not enter lab queues until physical intake is confirmed.
problems.action: Locate the physical soil bag, inspect and weigh it in Sample Reception, and click Complete Intake (or Accept & Print Label).

steps: Open Sample Reception, choose Project Sample, Walk-in / External, or Consignment Batch, and scan or type the bag ID in 1. ID & Field. (Expected: If the sample was pre-registered from a field survey, its status shows Expected and its field details load automatically.)

Weigh the soil bag and complete 2. Condition by checking Container Intact / Sealed and Sample Quantity Sufficient. (Expected: Any damaged bag or low sample weight is flagged so you can add a condition note, quarantine the bag, or reject it.)

Verify the requested test package in 3. Analyses, then open 4. Handover and click Complete Intake (or Accept & Print Label). (Expected: The sample status moves from Expected to Accepted, barcode labels print, and drying tasks open in Workbench.)
articles.caution: Never click Complete Intake (or Accept & Print Label) without the physical soil bag in front of you.

articles.title: Your first shift as a laboratory manager
articles.summary: Manage your daily laboratory queues across intake exceptions, work assignment, batch review, and final sample approval.
articles.quick: Check Dashboard and Manager Task List each morning to assign pending tests, review submitted technician runs in Review Submissions, approve completed samples in Final Approvals, and issue PDF reports in Reports.
before: Confirm your active laboratory name in the top bar.
Remember that when your laboratory enables Require a second reviewer in Policies, you cannot approve a run that you recorded yourself.

steps.action: Open Dashboard and Manager Task List to check queue counts for unassigned work, Review Submissions, and Final Approvals.
steps.expected: You see all batches waiting for technical review and all samples waiting for final sign-off in your laboratory.

steps.action: Open Review Submissions to inspect technician batch values and quality control results, then click Approve or Return.
steps.expected: Approved determinations advance toward sample completion, while returned items open a fresh repeat attempt on the technician's bench with your note.

steps.action: Open Final Approvals to check whole-sample plausibility across all tests, approve the sample, and issue the Certificate of Analysis in Reports.
steps.expected: The sample status moves to Approved and its official PDF report is ready to download or share.

fields: Review Submissions
Stage 1 review tab in Manager Task List for method batches
Check instrument calibration, blanks, duplicates, and reference soil recovery here.
Final Approvals
Stage 2 review tab in Manager Task List for complete samples
Check cross-parameter agreement across all finished tests before final release.
Reports
Menu item that opens Result Reports for generating Certificates of Analysis
Use this screen to issue new PDF reports or start a formal report amendment.
articles.example: In Manager Task List, review and approve a submitted Olsen P batch in Review Submissions, then approve sample DEMO-001 in Final Approvals and generate its PDF report in Reports.
articles.success: Submitted bench work is reviewed promptly, failed runs are returned with clear instructions, and approved samples are ready for reporting.
articles.nextActor: Laboratory Technician (for returned work) or Client / Project Manager (for issued reports)

problems.symptom: A technician says a batch is finished, but nothing appears in Review Submissions.
problems.why: The technician saved or recorded the values in Workbench without clicking Submit in Ready to Submit, or a queue filter is active.
problems.action: Clear any active filters in Manager Task List and ask the technician to check Ready to Submit and Sent & Completed in Workbench.

steps: Open Dashboard and Manager Task List to check queue counts for unassigned work, Review Submissions, and Final Approvals. (Expected: You see all batches waiting for technical review and all samples waiting for final sign-off in your laboratory.)

articles.title: Follow a project through the laboratory

articles.quick: Open Projects to view how many samples in your project are Expected, Accepted, Processing, Submitted, or Approved, and see which role owns the next step.
before: Confirm that your user account has access to the project and laboratory in the top bar.
Keep your project code or consignment list handy when filtering large surveys.

steps.action: Open Projects from the side menu and select your project card.
steps.expected: The project summary shows total samples and progress counts for each stage of the laboratory journey.

steps.action: Compare the Expected count (synced from field forms) with the Accepted and Processing counts.
steps.expected: You can immediately tell which field bags are still in transit and which bags have arrived at Sample Reception.

Samples registered from field forms that have not physically arrived at the lab yet

articles.title: Inspect laboratory work without changing it
articles.summary: Inspect sample evidence, quality control charts, non-conformances, and audit trails in read-only mode.

before: Sign in with your Quality & Audit Officer or auditor account and check your laboratory scope in the top bar.
Have the sample ID, batch number, or Certificate of Analysis report number you want to trace.

steps.action: Open Sample Registry, search for the sample ID, and inspect its Overview, Work & results, and Chain of Custody tabs.
steps.expected: You see the complete history of intake condition, drying and sieving receipts, measurement attempts, and storage moves.

steps.action: Open QA Dashboard to inspect Control charts, Non-Conformance records, Proficiency Testing rounds, and the Audit Log.
steps.expected: Every quality control check, failed-batch decision, and setting change is displayed with who did it, when, and why.

steps.action: Open Reports to compare the Current Certificate of Analysis with any Withdrawn or Superseded revisions.

articles.example: Trace sample DEMO-001 from its Certificate of Analysis in Reports back to its Attempt 1 and Attempt 2 bench records and linked Non-Conformance entry in QA Dashboard.

before: Sign in with your viewer or client account.
Check which project or laboratory is selected in your filter bar.

steps.action: Open Sample Registry or Data & Results and filter by your project name or sample ID.
steps.expected: You see all samples shared with your account and their current stage in the laboratory.

steps.expected: Only approved samples with issued Certificates of Analysis appear for download.

fields: Current
Badge indicating the active, official version of a Certificate of Analysis
Always use the Current report version for agronomic recommendations.
Superseded
Badge indicating an older report that was replaced by an amended version
Do not use a Superseded PDF; download the newest Current revision instead.
Withdrawn
Badge shown while an issued report is temporarily pulled back for correction
Wait until the laboratory issues the replacement Current report.
articles.example: Open Reports, filter for project SOILFER-DEMO, verify the report badge says Current, and download the PDF Certificate of Analysis.

articles.title: Enter qualifiers and missing results correctly
articles.summary: Record below-detection readings (< LOD, < LOQ) properly and never type zero for an unmeasured sample.
articles.quick: When a sample reading is below your method's detection or quantification limit, select the < LOD or < LOQ qualifier on the row instead of typing 0. If a sample was not measured in today's run, leave it blank and exclude it from today's submission.

articles.title: Understand partial submissions and partial reports
articles.summary: Understand the difference between a partial bench submission (some tests done) and a fully approved sample.
articles.quick: A sample often has fast tests (like pH) that finish days before slower tests (like particle-size texture). Technicians can submit finished tests early (Partially Done), and managers can review those runs in Review Submissions while the sample waits for its remaining tests before Final Approvals.

Check whether your laboratory policy allows interim partial reports or requires all tests to finish before issuing a Certificate of Analysis.

steps.expected: The approved determinations are locked and saved, while the overall sample badge shows Partially Done until the remaining tests arrive.

steps.action: Once the remaining bench tests are submitted and approved in Review Submissions, open Final Approvals to approve the complete sample.

Submitted

Progress
Scope breakdown shown in Ready to Submit and Review Submissions
Prevents anyone from mistaking a single-method approval for whole-sample completion.
articles.example: Approve the submitted pH and EC batch for DEMO-26-000142 on Tuesday (sample shows Partially Done), then approve the hydrometer texture panel on Thursday and complete Final Approvals.
articles.success: Fast bench methods are reviewed without bottlenecking the lab, and whole-sample approval waits until every ordered test is accounted for.

articles.title: Recover from a blank page or failed application update (manage-load-error)
articles.summary: Protect drafts and use verified retry/update behavior before escalating. [Canonical successor: quality-loading]
articles.quick: Protect drafts and use verified retry/update behavior before escalating. [Canonical successor: quality-loading] Use /help to inspect the full before/after Audit Log, evaluate batch QC alerts and Shewhart control charts, open and track Non-Conformance Reports (NCR / CAPA), trace repeat attempts (R1, R2) and Report Revisions (Rev 1, Rev 2), or safely recover from browser/update errors.
before: Identify the exact Laboratory Sample Code, Batch ID, Report Number (RPT-...), or timestamp involved.
If recovering from a loading error on a bench device, do not clear browser storage before checking for unsynchronized offline drafts.

steps.action: Open /help and filter by sample code, batch ID, actor, date range, or alert status.
steps.expected: The complete chronological evidence trail loads—including raw attempts, QC evaluations, policy snapshots, and report revisions.

steps.action: Inspect the quality evidence or execute the recovery step (Protect drafts and use verified retry/update behavior before escalating. [Canonical successor: quality-loading]).
steps.expected: You can distinguish an automated file-upload check from analytical batch QC (BLANK, DUPLICATE, LRM, CRM, ICV/CCV), and trace every repeat (R1 → R2) or amended report (WITHDRAWN / SUPERSEDED → Rev 2).

steps.action: Record the required QC disposition, Non-Conformance Report (NCR) root cause and corrective action, or support ticket with minimal non-sensitive evidence.
steps.expected: Quality decisions and CAPA actions are permanently linked to the affected batch or sample without silently overwriting historical data.

fields: Analytical Batch QC vs. Import Check
QC_PASS / QC_WARN / QC_FAIL on RunBatch
File parsing success only means the file was readable; batch approval requires passing analytical QC or a Manager caveat disposition.
Non-Conformance Report (NCR)
Required when attempts exceed repeats.maxAttemptsBeforeNcr or on major deviations
Documents description, root cause, containment, and corrective action (CAPA) before closure.
Report Lineage (Rev 1 → Rev 2)
ISSUED, WITHDRAWN, SUPERSEDED states
Public QR links immediately stop serving WITHDRAWN/SUPERSEDED PDFs and display a plain-text notice.
articles.example: In /qa, open failed batch BATCH-2026-0414, log NCR-2026-009 ("Olsen P reagent contamination in Blank"), trigger Repeat Batch (R2), and verify closure.
articles.success: Quality evidence, audit lineage, NCR corrective actions, or application recovery steps are completed with full traceability.
articles.nextActor: Quality Manager, Laboratory Manager, or Technical Support

problems.action: Follow the linked Batch ID or Sample ID in /qa and /admin/audit, verify the latest Report Revision in /result-reports, and preserve unsynced drafts before reloading the app.
